newsitem.title: USA: RAIN FALLS IN ILLINOIS, INDIANA, MORE FORECAST-WSC.
newsitem.headline: RAIN FALLS IN ILLINOIS, INDIANA, MORE FORECAST-WSC.

text.p: Corn and soybean crops in the driest areas of Illinois and Indiana received only light weekend showers but more rain is forecast, Weather Services Corp senior agricultural meteorologist Joel Burgio said.
"Even though we haven't had a lot of the driest areas of Illinois and Indiana improve during the weekend we still have the potential that they may in the next 24 to 48 hours," Burgio said.
"Assuming the forecast for the next 48 hours verifies it looks like it (the rainfall) would have been heavier and more widespread than expected," he added.
Burgio said rains of 0.50 to 1.50 inches were forecast for the Missouri, Illinois, Indiana and Ohio region during the next 24 to 48 hours, with around 60 percent coverage.
"I think the corn crop will be less likely to improve significantly based on the rainfall due to some pollination problems but the soybean crop could improve significantly," WSC's Burgio said.
He said that so far only about 30 percent of the driest areas of central Illinois and central Indiana had received more than 0.50 inch rain.

More significant rain fell overnight in a band from the Iowa-Illinois border eastward covering the more northerly 30 to 40 percent of Illinois. Weekend rains in Peoria, Ill., totalled 1.73 inches and in Moline, Ill., 1.54 inches.
There were also showers in south-east Nebraska and the extreme west of Iowa of 0.30 to 1.00 inch, locally heavier with Grand Island, Neb., receiving 3.15 inches over the weekend.

On Wednesday, showers may linger in far east portions of the corn belt and conditions would be mostly dry on Thursday. Showers were expected to return to the Western Corn Belt on Friday and over the weekend, Burgio said.
